why: A (universes at 0) is about the project's specific construction W ×_{W'} W'' := wfpSEP hΦ Ψ = πZ*W'', with ΠZ = projZ and ΠX = projX. Its conjuncts: theorem_10_2_2 (projZ is a strong bundle equivalence, projX ≫ Φ ≃ projZ ≫ Ψ, the legs cover πX and πZ); theorem_10_2_2_right; nonempty_wfpSEP; two general lemmas (isStrongBundleEquivalence_pullbackProjFunctor: the pull-back along an equivalence projects by a strong bundle equivalence; SEP.natEquiv_cone); and an example. B is existential: SOME strong bundle C with legs πW, πW₂ and an EP-isomorphism of C's base with wfp Φ.ϕ Ψ.ϕ h, with the covering equations, πW₂ an equivalence, πW ≫ Φ ≃ πW₂ ≫ Ψ, and πW an equivalence if Ψ is one. A ⇒ B (rt_check OK) takes C = wfpSEP, e = Iso.refl (structure eta, and proof irrelevance for the Prop Admissible), the covering equations by rfl, and the rest from theorem_10_2_2(_right). B ⇒ A fails for a genuine reason. B pins down only the base of its C up to isomorphism, not the total space or the legs, so nothing it says transfers to the project's projX/projZ. The general pull-back and cone lemmas and the example are not consequences of B either. Deriving them would mean re-proving the construction outright. On the text's (unstated) claim the two sides agree; A adds a concrete construction and the lemmas behind it.
overlap: No B_to_A, so no rt_overlap. #rt_check OK on A_to_B.
